nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sea level rise|Saltwater intrusion into freshwater aquifers_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the main risks associated with the ICUW as identified in the study?
nodes.answer: The ICUW is vulnerable to contamination from agricultural runoff, seawater intrusion, and geothermal water intrusion.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Urban wetlands provide vital ecological services, yet their hydrogeochemical dynamics and associated risks remain insufficiently explored, espe- cially within urban contexts. This study aims to evalu- ate the Inciralti-Cakalburnu Urban Wetland (ICUW) in Izmir, Turkey, as a case study for understanding the complex interactions between water quality, contamina- tion risks, and urban development. The ICUW, a unique example of a natural coastal urban wetland, offers criti- cal services such as flood regulation, water purification, and carbon sequestration, while also being vulnerable to contamination from agricultural runoff, seawater and geothermal water intrusion. Key findings include significant variations in water quality parameters: pH values range from 6.73 to 9.0, electrical conductivity (EC) from 911 to 61,700 S/cm, and total dissolved sol- ids (TDS) from 631 to 42,935 mg/L. Notably, concen- trations of heavy metals such as arsenic (0.2 0.48 mg/L), boron (0.60 39.6 mg/L), bromide (0.100 80.8 mg/L), fluoride (0.130 4.2 mg/L) and nitrate (0.5 193 mg/L) exceed recommended levels, posing health risks.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sea level rise|Saltwater intrusion into freshwater aquifers_qna_006
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What percentage of the north-western Black Sea area was impacted by the dam breach?
nodes.answer: More than 50% of the area of the north-western Black Sea was impacted by the dam breach.
nodes.paragraph: communications earth & environment Article A Nature Portfolio journal https://doi.org/10.1038/s43247-25-2153-z The biogeochemical response of the north-western Black Sea to the KakhovkaDam breach Check for updates Dalin Jiang1, Valeriy Khokhlov1,2, Yurii Tuchkovenko3, Dmytro Kushnir4, Valeriya Ovcharuk5, Evangelos Spyrakos1,A drianStanica6 Violeta Slabakova7& Andrew Tyler1 The Kakhovka Dam explosion is an example of the far-reaching environmental consequences of warfare. The resulting dam collapse released some 14.4 billion cubic meters of water, ooding downstream environments and ushing unknown quantities of debris, pollutants and sediments into the north-western Black Sea. With a combined satellite and hydrological modelling approach, supported with in situ data, we assessed the short-term impact on the north-western Black Sea. Thedam breach impacted more than 50% of the area of the north-western Black Sea, experiencing over 50times the ambient Chlorophyll- aand suspended sediment concentrations. Signi cant increases of nitrate and phosphate were also observed in the Odesa coastal environment. This environmentalshock triggered severe algal blooms within one week, that persisted for a further 20 days. This eventmay have impacted the biodiversity of the north-western Black Sea and its ecosystem response.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sea level rise|Saltwater intrusion into freshwater aquifers_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the main environmental stressors affecting samphires and their habitats as identified in the document?
nodes.answer: The main environmental stressors affecting samphires and their habitats include drought, flooding, heat stress, wind, water extraction, secondary salinization, habitat fragmentation, and mining, all of which threaten the integrity of salt lake ecosystems.
nodes.paragraph: These communities provide ecological benefits such as filtering runoff to marine areas, and habitat for birds and many other species including rare and threatened taxa (DEE 2017). Samphires also contribute to soil stabilisation, range- land pastoral production, ecotourism and biodiversity conservation (Williams 2002; DEE 2017), and are utilised both as a human food source and for medicinal purposes (Srivara- than et al. 2021). While samphires are considered robust plants due to their ability to thrive and grow in harsh conditions, they are adapted to specific and often narrow environmental niches which make them vulnerable to changes in those conditions (Datson 2002). Their distribution is largely influenced by fluctuations in salinity, water availability and tempera- ture, with their survival determined by tolerances to extreme conditions (Koull & Chehma 2014; Chenchouni 2017; Contreras-Cruzado et al. 2017). As salinity and waterlogging lev - els change rapidly with variations in hydrology, salt lakes are particularly vulnerable to the effects of climate change (Jellison et al. 2008). Recent reports by the Intergovernmen- tal Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) (2022) indicate arid climate zones are highly vulner - able to climate change and have been affected globally, influenced by intermittent rainfall and increased temperatures.

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What gap in knowledge is highlighted concerning water boundary conditions and their interactions with FTCs?
nodes.answer: There remains a notable gap in knowledge regarding the influence of water boundary conditions and their interactions with FTCs.
nodes.paragraph: observed a significant reduction in load- bearing capacity when water was sprayed on beam (1.2 0.25 0.15 m3) surfaces during FTCs [20]. Other experiments involved smaller specimens (sec- tional size of 100 mm) entirely submerged in water [4, 21 24], with few studies directly comparing dif- ferent water boundary conditions and their interac- tions with FTCs. Thus, there remains a notable gap in knowledge regarding the influence of water boundary conditions. To better understand internal frost damage in concrete, dual-scale experimental studies are essential. Here, "dual-scale" refers to investiga- tions encompassing both macro-scale and meso- scale. At the macro-scale (structural or compo- nent level, above 10 mm), concrete is considered a homogenised material, whereas at the meso-scale (material level, 15 mm), it is necessary to distin- guish the individual constituents of concrete, such as aggregates and the cementitious matrix [25]. At the macro-scale, mechanical tests, such as wedge- splitting and compression tests, assess the impact of frost damage on tensile strength/fracture behav - iour and compressive strength, respectively [4, , 11, 12, 26 31].
